item.title: Thoughts
item.content:encoded:
I'm really nobody important, but I figured I'd give my thoughts on a two-year-old article anyway. Just to preface, I really like this article, but it seems a bit uncharacteristic. Unless the anomaly affects everyone's minds to make them at peace about the end of the world, wouldn't the Foundation try to counteract the end of the world. I mean, something being inevitable hasn't stopped them from at least attempting it before.

Also, I think that a bit more should be added (mainly who discovered it and how) but other than that I like the brevity and self-explanation of the article.

item.title: Re: ._/(.-.)\_.
item.content:encoded:
+ Discussion of Apollyon that was longer than I intended
– hide block

Yeah, the class' sheer saturation has removed whatever feelings of dread/fear which initially came with it. Adding Apollyon to the article now also adds a whole other burden to the author, to justify the usage of Apollyon, which this proposal neither wants to engage with nor really can engage with given its brevity.

Also, as the resident "maintainer" of the esoterics list, I can say it's not really that simple. The only articles to use Apollyon at the time of this proposal's publication were SCP-3999, S. D. Locke's Proposal, and SCP-2317 — although Clef had purged the class from 2317 two months previous. Apollyon was not yet a fixture of site culture and would only undergo a period of commodification mid-way through 2018, several months after Lily posted this. At the time, Apollyon not only denoted an article about the end of the world, but an article concerned with the eldritch, with dead gods, with the imminent and unrelenting inevitability of mankind's destruction — which is not Lily's Proposal.

Even by modern standards your implementation of Apollyon is inaccurate, since it doesn't only mean the object is uncontainable but that it presents an active threat. In this case, SCP-001 is essentially a passive and beneficial phenomenon incidentally triggered by the end of the world — for which containment is capital-U Unnecessary.

item.title: Re: Out of character
item.content:encoded:
I see your point and I don't want to necro, but

They know they've failed their mission, and there's no coming back from it, this time.

My guy/gal/pal I can instantly think of dozens of solutions to this death
2000 has definitively solved multiple XKs, and that's not even my first solution.
Reality evasion, space side assets,

all life on the planet.

Predictive Everett Algorithms or Cross Ion Trap comms to find out the difference between the realities. Hell, it says life, that may not include comatose or cryostorage. Exclusionary Site seeded with pockets of life, Drop pods, ready to reseed the earth, and guns pointed at the gods, demanding a fix.
If I can easily avoid this thing, the goddamn motherf*cking Foundation? You bet your last bottle of booze, they can, and will. Humanity has always seen it's problems as a starting point, a list to solve, and the Foundation embodies and personifies humanity's will to survive, beyond even our reality.

Doesn't really do much for me. It's short and it tries to hit, but for me, it just feels off, somehow. I doubt the Foundation would just be like,

"Welp, this is going to happen so, pfffffff. 173 go weeeeeeeeeeeeeeee"

It doesn't feel like a 001 proposal, it doesn't feel like a scip. I could see it as a pretty great tale, and I appreciate the new take on 001, contrasted with the maximalist style used in the other 001 scips, but it doesn't feel like it used it. Plenty of other people have said what I have said and probably far better. If you enjoyed writing it that's cool. I'm glad other people like it, and it showed me an interesting take on scips in general. Not my headcanon, and as I said, it doesn't feel like a scip, 001 or otherwise.

I also kind of feel like this had a lot of potential and then just stood there, waiting for me to feel better? Or worse? Or scared? I can't tell the intention behind this article, tbh.

+ Actual criticism if you're into that stuff
- Hugs

Hey, thanks for reading this. IDK how long that'll be so we'll find out together. It might be nitpicky, I'm biased, I admit, but I'm trying to go with the style of this scip in my crit. These are all suggestions and, hey, you got your scip this far, you don't need them, just tiny improvements from my POV.

One of my first main problems

Object Class: Unnecessary

Now I know it may be a trope in 001 SCPs to have an esoteric class, and it's stark, don't get me wrong, this drew my attention like a magnet, but you didn't use that hook. Besides, we already have a class for this. Apollyon, you can just use that. It has the same draw, it juxtaposes with other Apollyon scps and doesn't fall into the trap of "Well it's 001, it must be a special class and all that."

Second thingy:

all personnel, including D-class, are to be honorably discharged

Now I get what you're going for. Or at least I think I do. But the Foundation isn't the military. They don't honorably discharge. Retired, laid off? It feels really off to me and not Foundation. I mean the whole thing isn't Foundation, but it's your headcanon.
Also also: D-class? All of them? They mostly are rapists, serial murders. These are death row inmates, capital offenses. You have the 512 things and

They will also experience heavily decreased levels of violence.

But if you have that, firstly, a little redundant. That's what 512 does so do they not know if the CK causes a reduction or do they want to reduce the reduced?

Either way, it's a little confusing, but you also have:

All sapient and non-aggressive SCPs are to be released.

Now firstly is it only the

  • both sapient and non-aggressive or
  • all sapients and all non-aggressive or
  • all sapient and non-aggressive and other non-aggressive.

B/c that's confusingly worded. For example, both 682 and the plague doctor are both sapient/sentient but I wouldn't want them running around at the end of the world, while 999 is definitively non-aggressive, but seems to have similar intelligence to a socially adjusted dog.
Now if 682 and 049 are both pacified by the end of the world then just say:

They will also experience a complete cessation of violence.

It hits just as hard if not harder than a "heavily decreased level," and while I'm on the sentence, please don't start one with "They will also…," you're starting out stumbling, it's like saying, "And another thing!" or "And with you as well."
Try:

This causes…

or

The population likewise…

And the same goes for

Air pollution will additionally clear.

You could combine this or split off a bit of the sentence before this, but it feels like you just wrote it in one afternoon.

Any further SCPs which can be decommissioned are to be.

Now, what is meant by decommissioned? Like executed decommissioned? It's a tone break, from peaceful oblivion to silent holocaust(Which I would also totally read.) Because you already used released, so I and other readers are led to assume this is something different

I digress of course. my other issue with this is if this causes the world to be some temporary utopia, which it seems to be implying, then why are only people affected? To go back to my earlier hypothetical, would 682 be all happy and smiles?

I would also link to something for the AIAD, not everyone knows what those are, and additional reading is nice.

Are the exclusionary sites unaffected? That is their one and only purpose, to block reality-altering changes. Your Foundation, at least in this article, seems to kind of give up? Like, "Well this might as well happen." Aside from being completely jarring, and not at all in line with most interpretations, are they just going to shut down 2000? Our Deus Ex Machina?

…before the death of all life on the planet.

The Foundation has spaceside assets, as does the rest of the world. I would see a scramble for space and for those in space new plans to survive when the planet doesn't. It looks like everyone on the ISS would just starve to death, and the Foundation spaceside would too. That's more depressing than the rest of this article, knowing that all their friends and loved ones died, without them. Just stranding them in space.

The rest of it was really good though, especially with the song, it felt like it could punch me in the gut. Maybe more words, maybe less. Your style.

Now I'm biased, I strongly dislike this scip. It's far too short, it had a great premise, but it feels a bit like if a comedian came on stage, said one great joke and then stared at you for the rest of the hour. Wasn't exactly executed like a Captain Jack Sparrow, but it wasn't My Immortal. It's a tad too happy for me, I watch Markiplier and read when I want to feel happy, but as dumb as this may sound to you, I come to this site to be scared. To know(or worse to not know) that the horrors abound, that the tickle on your neck is the breath of a spine eating monster. That every shadow holds a secret, it'll tell you if you lean in. That the eyes you feel boring into the back of your skull, have been there longer than you have noticed them. That every black bar was etched by a madman as the horror consumed his dregs of sanity. That the multiverse and time herself, marched on dragging your bloated corpse across the river Styx, as Charon asked for your only coin.

+ show block
– hide block

So, obviously, not my cup of tea, or in my case, not my cup of indescribable horror screaming from the great beyond. With the song you added, I can better see what you were going for, but might I humbly suggest a format break. Perhaps a tale from one of the alternate universes, maybe a short addendum or you could actually have the

attached document 001-A

Unless you already did, and I can't find it in which case, thanks!

The vibe I was hoping for was silent holocaust where humanity was memetically pacified so we wouldn't resist our inevitable demise, but what I got was: Oh Lalala, lovely apocalypse today.

Either way, thanks for reading my stuff as I read yours, and can you link to some of that stuff in your headcanon? It seems sweet.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

I upvoted this a long while ago but I don't think I ever commented. This is really competing for my favorite article on the site. Every time I read it I cry, but not because I'm sad. It gives me peace, and somehow makes me feel more capable of hoping as well. It's a beautiful work. To me, this is an incredibly important piece of art.

item.title: Beautiful
item.content:encoded:
I find this proposal just, enchanting, I think. The lack of length isn't an issue, 001 may be important but I don't believe length or substance is paramount. You conveyed an idea that supersedes all else in the Foundation, it's the light at the end of an infinitely dark tunnel. The foundation's job has been done, and now, they can finally take a deep breath, and relax.

They work in the dark so humanity can live in the light, and finally, that light is shining down on everyone.

That's how I see it at least, this proposal is a beautiful work of art that not just lays out a concept that is by itself paradigmatic, but also provokes feelings, and thoughts. Non hostile sentient scps going free is no longer a breach, it's the foundation finally letting them have their peace, in the final day. So many anomalies in the foundation are simply creatures we can't understand, that just want to live. Having read all the scps like that that I have, it encourages further thought and consideration. Take, for example, scp 1824. Without the -1, it shows no anomalous properties. It simply wishes to be free. It's only one example of hundreds, and I think this proposal is amazing. It draws attention to the foundation as a whole, and to the entities within. I'd upvote more than once if I could, amazing job.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hmm… good story, overall, it's just that, well…

I find it a bit unrealistic. I mean, the Foundation motto isn't Surrender, Concede, Pause1. If I had to equate the Foundation with something, I would probably put it as a cockroach or something.

Seriously, the Foundation's survived homicidal lizards, zombie plagues, and they still haven't given up. But then this comes up, an actual 24 hour early prediction to the planet's end… and nothing? No plans to escape the planet by going to another planet, or running through to another dimension… just giving up?

I mean, sure, if the planet's automatically forcing them to give up and accept their fate when that event occurs, I'd understand, but I'd expect them to just set up an escape system that'll automatically make them escape and then wipe their own memories to prevent themselves from 'accepting their fate' and destroying their escape paths.

Now, if the SCP in question is actually already influencing them to just give up and accept their fate, that'd add a slight more bit of truth, but, I'd expect some people to resist at the very least.

Now, granted, it's a drop of light in an ocean of despair and misery. *Looks around at basically every other SCP-001 entry*. Scratch that. It's one of the very, very few drops of light in an ocean of despair and misery.

I don't know about this one… I won't downvote this, but I won't upvote this either.

Footnotes
1. Totally didn't spend a couple of minutes thinking of a motto that fit 'SCP'.

item.title: Re: Out of character
item.content:encoded:
That's the point; They always go at the worst scenarios Guns-A-Blazin' because they all swore an oath to do whatever in their power they can to protect Earth, no matter the cost. And that's the eerie part.

The Foundation; when All the Sarkic Gods with their infinite power come to snap them out of existence; when the fucking writers of everything they do appear to them and throw at them instant world ending reptiles, they don't "Get peaceful and die" no, they go full fucking petal to the metal, they work up until that last nanosecond of existence, they're not going to let out all the SCPs and D-Class, they need those for any last minute tests, they're not going to tell their scientists "we can't prevent the end, it's over, go home" NO! They're gonna need every bit of knowledge for some last minute experiments or ideas. They don't give half a shit if the multiverse is about to end by The Scarlet King. They're going to do everything they can to keep Humanity alive.

Here; they finally give up, this event is fate itself; which they have defied so many times, finally telling them "It's over. Your work is done. Go do what you want, but it's all over for you." Usually they'd say "Fuck off, mate" and keep on hammering down, but not this time.

I think this is what people tend to miss in a lot of things

The Foundation can't even muster up the stubbornness to keep on going until the last nanosecond, they just know it's over. And that they've done what they've needed to do. This proposal signifies the day the Foundation has failed their mission, their oath, and their code: Secure. Contain. Protect.

There's a deeper meaning to this SCP. It's not just "everything goes rosy for the last day of Earth".

It's the signification that the Foundation failed to do what they have done for so many years and succeeded.

And they don't even want to try and fight their own failure when it's there in front of them. They can't even muster up the strength to do whatever they need to do.

They know they've failed their mission, and there's no coming back from it, this time.

That's what makes this SCP truly amazing.
